title: Device peaks
brief: Derive peak FLOP/s, bandwidth, and ridge points from SM counts, clocks, and HBM geometry for the A100, H100, and B200, then check the A100 numbers against a real matmul on the lab card.
hints: A tensor core does a fixed number of fused multiply-adds per clock, and one FMA is 2 FLOP. Multiply tensor cores per SM, FMAs per tensor core per clock, and 2 to get FLOP per SM per clock for bf16.
The other precisions are ratios of the bf16 rate: tf32 is 0.5, fp8 is 2, and fp4 is 4. The fp32 rate is the CUDA cores, not a tensor core: fp32_lanes_per_sm times 2.
Peak FLOP/s is SMs x FLOP per SM per clock x clock. Mind the units: a clock in MHz is 1e6 cycles per second, and the function returns TFLOP/s, which is 1e12.
Bandwidth in GB/s is bus width in bits times pin rate in Gb/s, divided by 8. To recover the pin rate from the rating, run the same formula backwards.

The matmul measurements need a GPU. Without one, the tests still check every formula and skip the measurement. On the lab A100, a large bf16 matmul lands well below the 312 TFLOP/s peak, and your lab reports the fraction.
